style_1_icd10.name: Impetigo, unspecified
style_1_icd10.chapter: XII. Diseases of the skin and subcutaneous tissue / Dermatology (L00-L99)

style_3_monograph.summary: Impetigo is a skin infection caused by bacteria. It is usually caused by staphylococcal (staph) bacteria, but it can also be caused by streptococcal (strep) bacteria. It is most common in children between the ages of two and six. It usually starts when bacteria get into a break in the skin, such as a cut, scratch, or insect bite. Symptoms start with red or pimple-like sores surrounded by red skin. These sores can be anywhere, but usually they occur on your face, arms and legs. The sores fill with pus, then break open after a few days and form a thick crust. They are often itchy, but scratching them can spread the sores. Impetigo can spread by contact with sores or nasal discharge from an infected person. You can treat impetigo with antibiotics.
style_3_monograph.treatment: Your provider will usually prescribe antibiotics that you need to take by mouth (oral antibiotics). Very early cases may be treated with antibiotics that you apply to the affected area (topical antibiotics). Serious infections may need antibiotics given through a vein (intravenous antibiotics). Placing a warm, wet cloth over the area can help remove ulcer crusts. Your provider may recommend antiseptic soap or peroxide washes to speed recovery.

approved_molecules.name: MUPIROCIN
approved_molecules.indication_snippet: Indicated for the treatment of impetigo and secondary skin infections, leading to traumatic skin lesions, due to _Staphylococcus aureus_ and _Streptococcus pyogenes_.

approved_molecules.name: OZENOXACIN
approved_molecules.indication_snippet: Ozenoxacin cream is indicated for the topical treatment of impetigo caused by *Staphylococcus aureus* or *Streptococcus pyogenes* in patients aged 2 months of age and older.
